pairs: Addidit quoque Job,
Job also added to this,
assumens parabolam suam,
using figures of speech,
et dixit:
and he said:
Quis mihi tribuat ut sim juxta menses pristinos,
Who will grant to me that I might be as I was in former months,
secundum dies quibus Deus custodiebat me?
according to the days when God kept watch over me?
Quando splendebat lucerna ejus super caput meum,
At that time, his lamp shined over my head,
et ad lumen ejus ambulabam in tenebris:
and by his light, I walked through the darkness.
sicut fui in diebus adolescentiæ meæ,
I was then just as in the days of my youth,
quando secreto Deus erat in tabernaculo meo:
when God was privately in my tabernacle.
quando erat Omnipotens mecum,
At that time,
et in circuitu meo pueri mei:
the Almighty was with me and my children surrounded me.
quando lavabam pedes meos butyro,
Then, I washed my feet with butter,
et petra fundebat mihi rivos olei:
and a boulder poured out rivers of oil for me.
quando procedebam ad portam civitatis,
When I went to the gate of the city,
et in platea parabant cathedram mihi.
or to the main street, they prepared a chair for me.
Videbant me juvenes, et abscondebantur:
The youths saw me and hid themselves, and the elders,
et senes assurgentes stabant.
rising up, remained standing.
Principes cessabant loqui,
The leaders stopped talking,
et digitum superponebant ori suo.
and they placed a finder over their mouth.
Vocem suam cohibebant duces,
The commanders subdued their voice,
et lingua eorum gutturi suo adhærebat.
and their tongue adhered to their throat.
Auris audiens beatificabat me,
The ear that heard me, blessed me,
et oculus videns testimonium reddebat mihi:
and the eye that saw me, gave testimony for me.
eo quod liberassem pauperem vociferantem,
This was because I had freed the poor, who cried out,
et pupillum cui non esset adjutor.
and the orphan, who had no helper.
Benedictio perituri super me veniebat,
The blessing of him who would have been destroyed came upon me,
et cor viduæ consolatus sum.
and I consoled the heart of the widow.
Justitia indutus sum,
I put on justice,
et vestivi me,
and I clothed myself with my judgment,
sicut vestimento et diademate,
like a robe
judicio meo.
and a diadem.
Oculus fui cæco,
I was an eye for the blind
et pes claudo.
and a foot for the lame.
Pater eram pauperum,
I was the father of the poor;
et causam quam nesciebam diligentissime investigabam.
and if I lacked knowledge about any case, I investigated very diligently.
Conterebam molas iniqui,
I crushed the jaws of the impious,
et de dentibus illius auferebam prædam.
and I took away prey from his teeth.
Dicebamque:
And I said,
In nidulo meo moriar,
“I will die in my little nest,
et sicut palma multiplicabo dies.
and like a palm tree, I will multiply my days.
Radix mea aperta est secus aquas,
My root has been spread beside the waters,
et ros morabitur in messione mea.
and the dew will remain with my harvest.
Gloria mea semper innovabitur,
My glory will always be restored,
et arcus meus in manu mea instaurabitur.
and my bow will be restored to my hand.”
Qui me audiebant,
Those who heard me,
expectabant sententiam,
expected vindication,
et intenti tacebant ad consilium meum.
and they listened closely in silence to my counsel.
Verbis meis addere nihil audebant,
To my words, they dared to add nothing,
et super illos stillabat eloquium meum.
and my eloquence poured over them.
Expectabant me sicut pluviam,
They waited for me as for rain,
et os suum aperiebant quasi ad imbrem serotinum.
and they opened their mouth as for belated rains.
Siquando ridebam ad eos,
If I had ever laughed at them,
non credebant:
they would not have believed it,
et lux vultus mei non cadebat in terram.
and the light of my face was not cast down towards the ground.
Si voluissem ire ad eos,
If I wished to go to them,
sedebam primus:
I sat down first,
cumque sederem quasi rex,
and,
circumstante exercitu,
though I sat like a king surrounded by an army,
eram tamen mœrentium consolator.
yet I was a comforter to those who mourned.
